hypotheses: Test whether the same fixed three-swap deployment package helps against an honest native opponent, using the original DOS army distribution as a controlled common deployment.
Separate an opponent-specific response from a deployment improvement that also transfers to an honest opponent.
analysis: Prespecified before cycle22 strength games or outcomes. Same three frozen policies, no retuning, original DOS-generated opponent armies and rotated sides. The opponent here uses honest guard moves and receives no private enemy setup. Its own army legitimately comes from the original DOS generator; this isolates move-opponent context from army distribution. Compare candidate-minus-control and candidate-minus-mixture effects. Absolute50% is NOT a fair-null benchmark because deployment distributions differ. Three contrasts are exploratory; report95% and98.3333% intervals; independent DOS validation needed before promotion.
evidence: Frozen cycle22 designs and mechanistic evidence only. Both players are honest; generator private seed is referee-only. This is auxiliary honest-opponent validation, not another DOS strength result.
